water and tillage contribute substantially to total erosion and that landscape segmentation can be used to identify areas of high erosion and to target soil and water conservation practices.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial and temporal variability of soil erosion in complex topography and the effects of soil erosion on crop production and soil properties.
the quantification of the spatial patterns of soil erosion and the identification of the major erosion processes on topographically complex agricultural landscapes.
the development and testing of a new conceptual framework to understand the spatial variability of water and tillge erosion in topographically-complex landscapes.

the relative importance of water and tillge erosion in the North American Prairies is dependent on the topography of the landscape, with the relative importance of the processes changing from site to site.

tillage erosion is the dominant process in hummocky landscapes while both tillage and water erosion are important in undulating landscapes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
landscape segmentation is an efficient tool for predicting soil erosion patterns and for designing conservation strategies.
landscape segmentation is a simple tool to represent spatially variable soil erosion and affected processes in topographically complex agricultural landscapes.

landscape segmentation can be used to identify and target soil conservation practices towards the most intensive erosion on given landform units.
